keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1994-2001: 'by 1994 they had gained control of much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province' (Sierra Leone page) and in 2001 'UN forces moved into rebel-held areas'. The extent for 1995-2000 is bridging: the pages record the January 1995 seizure of two mines in the southwest, the May 1997 AFRC/RUF capture of Freetown, ECOMOG's recapture in March 1998 and the January 1999 attack, but map none of it.

region.text: eastern Sierra Leone, across the Liberian border

ledger.note: 1991-03-23: the RUF invades from Liberia. The conflict 'began on 23 March 1991 when the Revolutionary United Front (RUF)' launched its intervention, backed by Charles Taylor's NPFL (the RUF page: it 'led elements of the National Patriotic Front of Liberia across the Liberian border'). The page does not name the district of entry, so the core is the Eastern Province.

ledger.note: 1991: the RUF takes the east and south. 'During the first year of the war, the RUF took control of large swathes of territory in eastern and southern Sierra Leone.'

ledger.note: 1994: the RUF holds the Eastern Province again. 'by 1994 they had gained control of much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province.' The RUF infobox names a 'Liberated Zone (1991-2002)' without a map.

ledger.note: 2002-01-18: the rebel-held areas return to the state. 'On 18 January 2002, President Kabbah declared the Sierra Leone Civil War over'; the 2001 UN disarmament moved into 'rebel-held areas' (Sierra Leone page). The ground held in 1995-2000 is not mapped on any page opened, so this region bridges a silence.

ledger.note: 2002-01-18: the war ends and the RUF ceases to hold land. 'On 18 January 2002, President Kabbah declared the Sierra Leone Civil War over'; afterwards the RUF 'was transformed into a political party: the Revolutionary United Front Party' (RUF page).

wars.name: Sierra Leone Civil War
belligerents: Liberia (Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia)

wars.outcome: The RUF lost: Kabbah declared the war over on 18 January 2002 and the movement became a political party; about 50,000 were killed between 1991 and 2001. Held the east and south in 1991, the Liberian border strip in 1993 and 'much of the diamond-rich Eastern Province' by 1994.
wars.note: Fully recorded in the sierra-leone dossier; the AFRC joined the RUF in a joint junta after the May 1997 coup, ended by ECOMOG in March 1998 (the RUF page says it 'was evicted from the capital by the intervention of a Nigerian-led West African force').

certainty.note: The rebel-held areas are described as 'large swathes' and 'much of' provinces; none of the pages opened gives a front line, a district list or an area.

notes: Revolutionary United Front: a rebel dossier written by af-08-i (a state Cliopatria lacks) because the RUF held land for years (rule 5). It rests on three pages and is thin: no page maps the ground it held between 1995 and 2000, the pages give no capital or headquarters (identity.capitals empty; Buedu and Kailahun are not on any page opened), no founding year before the invasion, and no list of leaders (Sankoh is named as founder, Issa Sesay appears only as a convicted leader in 2009). The regions are provinces and a border band, ceilings rather than outlines. A gap-filler should read the Sierra Leone Civil War article's sections on 1995-1997, the AFRC junta (May 1997 - March 1998) and the Lomé accord (7 July 1999 on one passage, 27 March 1999 on another) and refine the keyframes. wikidata is null (Wikidata is unreachable and Cliopatria has no row).
